close_reason: Added doc note on optional_arg explaining the ResultReference-null interaction. No behaviour change; the semantics is RFC-compliant. Future handler authors hitting the asymmetry will find the explanation in the rustdoc.
description:
crate-jmap-server/src/helpers.rs:64-78 — optional_arg collapses Value::Null and an absent key into None. Per RFC 8620 §3.3 (and the helper's own doc), this is correct: optional fields are equivalent in both cases.

But this interacts with ResultReference resolution in a non-obvious way. resolve_args (parse.rs:131) replaces a #key with the resolved value, and that value CAN be Value::Null when the JSON Pointer path resolves to an explicit null in the prior response's tree (RFC 6901 §4 makes no distinction between "key absent" and "key present with null"). When the resolved value is null, optional_arg treats it as absent — silently.

Scenario: a client calls Foo/query and the response contains `state: null`. The next call sends `#state: {resultOf: "c0", name: "Foo/query", path: "/state"}`. resolve_args succeeds, substituting `state: null` in args. optional_arg("state", ...) returns None. The handler proceeds as if state was not provided.

This is RFC-compliant but the asymmetry between "I sent an explicit null" and "I sent a ResultReference that resolved to null" is the kind of subtle behavior a contributor writing a new handler will not anticipate.

Action: add a doc note on optional_arg pointing at the resolve_args interaction. No behavior change — the semantics is correct, but a reader should be able to find the explanation when they hit it. One sentence linking the two helpers is sufficient.

Not a bug. Not actionable code-wise. Documentation gap that a maintainer will eventually hit.
title: optional_arg treats Value::Null and absent identically — masks ResultReference resolution to null
